RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel and selecting a candidate with fewer publications raises legitimate concerns about implicit bias, particularly given documented gender disparities in economics. However, hiring committees often prioritize specific subfield needs, interview performance, teaching evaluations, or industry background relevant to curriculum goals. 

Whether to raise the panel's composition depends on institutional policy and your desired outcome. Many public universities mandate gender-diverse search committees; if official hiring policy was breached, you have clear procedural grounds to query HR. Before making formal allegations, follow up on your requested feedback and review the university’s recruitment guidelines. If the feedback fails to provide objective justification, you can decide whether to consult a union representative or faculty ombudsperson.
